newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish bond market faces likely loss before Bos.
newsitem.headline: Spanish bond market faces likely loss before Bos.

text.p: Spanish bonos could go lower this week, as the consolidation mood could prevail after a fast run up and before appointments that could leave disappointment.

Dealers and economists said the market already discounted a 50 basis points cut in 7.25 percent key money rate and they said investors could show some delusion if Bank of Spain will prove itself more cautious than that.

"The market has already discounted a 50 basis point cut," Juan Antonio Mielgo economist at Bank of America in Madrid said. "But as I expect, Bank of Spain will do less, the market will push the yields up, above the eight percent in ten year bonds".

On Monday, December futures contract was trading at 1100 GMT at 106.29, 53 basis points lower than Friday's close. But dealers said the bonos were positioning for the Tuesday and Wednesday government auctions over three to 15 year bonds.

Earlier Spanish Treasury said it expects to sell around 275 billiones pesetas in three and ten year bond and 200 billiones in five and 15 years, for a total amount of 475. This is close of the 466 billions they sold at previous auction in September.
"In any case I do not expect the ten year future contract can go below 106 today or tomorrow," a dealer with Fimat saaid.
"If we will see something lower should be around 105.85".
What it is really worring, is the possibility Bank of Spain could be less generous then expected. "I do not rule out any level above 105 if the repo could be a disappointemt" Mielgo said.
But after the auctions, what the market is closely watching is the repo bank of Spain will offer next Thurday, the fisrt one after the Government has presented its 1997 budget.
"If Bank of Spain wont lower official rate on Thursday, the market will think they do not like the budget and this could be really dangerous" a dealer with a big istitution said to Reuter.
But even though Bank of Spain will limit its reduction in 25 basis points the market could decide to show more profit taking.
With September Cpi due on October 11, many analysts think Bank of Spain will be more prudent. "They can cut 25 points and then other 25 basis points before year end" Mielgo said.

But if this is what will happen the market could loose, specially on the short part of the curve. The 9.90 percent two year bonds trading at 105.50/53 and 6.93 this morning could go down with the yield above 7.05 percent, an economist said.
The 8.80 percent bond, trading this morning at 7.93 yield could go back above 8.00 percent level. It was sold just one month ago on September 3 at 8.921 percent.
